problem_type: Credential material presence conflated with enablement and verification
symptom: After an offline key save the UI says saved and not verified, but the persisted vendor projection reports hasApiKey=false. The display needs the saved-material fact without changing the availability primitive used by execution consumers.
direct_cause: The display projection had no material-only predicate, so pending disabled material was indistinguishable from no saved material in the renderer.
class_root: ApiKeyRecord.enabled is an execution/user-availability gate while verificationPending is a retry marker; treating material presence as the same fact changes decrypt status for every consumer. A full user-intent split requires a separate schema decision.
affected_population: Any probe-based vendor saved while network validation is inconclusive
Windows, macOS, or Linux users reopening a persisted pending credential
Every catalog reader that consumes the hasApiKey projection
entry_points: Catalog persistence projection keeps hasApiKey derived from apiKeyDecryptStatus and adds credentialMaterialSaved for display only.
Catalog availability checks enablement before decrypting or probing; pending health revalidation is the explicit verificationPending exception.
The key-only page maps credentialMaterialSaved, pending, and published facts to shared bilingual copy keys.
internal_only_reason: This is an application-level credential lifecycle invariant owned by the local catalog; Electron safeStorage remains unchanged and no provider protocol is being changed.
invariants: A non-empty persisted key record is exposed as credentialMaterialSaved even when enabled=false and verificationPending=true.
credentialRecordCounts and apiKeyDecryptStatus keep disabled records unavailable to decrypting consumers.
A disabled non-pending credential is never decrypted, probed, sent by a connector, or reported as available.
The UI says saved and not verified for pending material while hasApiKey remains the availability fact.
Every outbound decrypt goes through decryptApiKeyRecord, which refuses a disabled record before the keychain is opened; raw reads are the closed list in storedApiKeyReaders.test.ts.
The 'is a key stored' line follows the stored credential, not the replace-key form mode; an automatic re-check that clears pending changes the card to key confirmed, models not verified.

door_reduction.why_not: The 19 hasApiKey readers are presentation, health, onboarding, and generation consumers that must continue to consume the single availability projection; merging them would recreate parallel facts. The two credentialRecordCounts occurrences remain the shared readiness boundaries. The copy-key type and five credentialMaterialSaved readers/writer are separate renderer display boundaries and cannot be merged with availability without reintroducing the rejected semantic conflation. 2026-10-08 round 4: decryptApiKeyRecord had 21 doors that all decrypted without the enabled gate. They are merged at the owner instead of per caller: decryptApiKeyRecord itself now refuses disabled records, and the five callers that legitimately touch an unusable record (pending revalidation, candidate validation, key copy, user-triggered certification) use the named decryptStoredApiKeyRecord, a closed list pinned by storedApiKeyReaders.test.ts.

generality_proof: All checked readers receive the same Vendor projection from readCatalog. The 19 hasApiKey readers continue to see availability, while the key-only display consumes credentialMaterialSaved. Model availability converges on createCatalogAvailability; pending health revalidation is explicitly allowed only by verificationPending, so vendor, caller, platform, and persisted run do not change the disabled-key invariant.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Keep the existing usable/decryptable credential predicate; do not reinterpret disabled records.
Keep disabled credentials out of decrypt/probe and feed the shared availability owner.
Project hasApiKey as availability, credentialMaterialSaved as display metadata, and credentialVerificationPending once for every renderer and main-process reader.
Allow pending revalidation without probing a disabled non-pending credential.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The offline walk reads this persisted projection after reopening the page; it sees hasApiKey=false and credentialMaterialSaved=true for pending material.
The same pending record remains unusable while disabled, and the boundary avoids decrypt/probe until promotion.
The page consumes hasApiKey and credentialVerificationPending through the shared copy resolver, so saved pending material is rendered as saved and not verified.
Health probing consumes hasApiKey for usable records and explicitly permits verificationPending material; ordinary disabled records return unsupported before decrypt or request construction.
Decrypt now goes through the gated decryptApiKeyRecord and an empty key stops before any request; tikhubDisabledKey.test.ts proves a disabled record is not decrypted or probed.

recurrence.reason: Every network-inconclusive save can create enabled=false, verificationPending=true, and the same projection would previously misclassify it as missing.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs credentialRecordCounts -> secrets.ts and catalogModelAvailability.ts
rg -n hasApiKey electron src tests -> onboarding, health, generation, and recovery consumers

prevention.invariant: Material presence is exposed by credentialMaterialSaved for display; credentialRecordCounts and apiKeyDecryptStatus retain the existing availability semantics; disabled records are not probed except for explicit pending revalidation.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing material returns missing; locked or legacy material keeps its explicit decrypt status; disabled material remains unavailable to execution consumers while the pending display can still say saved.
prevention.strategy: Keep the existing readiness predicate stable, add one material-only display predicate, and make the pending health exception explicit instead of broadening decrypt status.

legacy_paths.rationale: No legacy writer or migration path is removed; existing persisted records keep their shape and are interpreted with separated material and availability facts.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The failure is in the application catalog invariant; Electron safeStorage and provider request dependencies are unchanged.

migration: No on-disk migration is needed for this bounded fix. Existing records keep apiKey, enabled, and optional verificationPending; readCatalog adds a derived display-only credentialMaterialSaved field. Splitting user intent from pending/verified state would require a separate schema migration and precedence decision for old enabled=false records.
residual_risks: The parallel F-vendorhealth2 line may change custom relay authorization-header precedence; this remediation deliberately does not alter verification request construction.
A pending credential remains unavailable to generation until the existing revalidation/promotion path enables it; health revalidation is the only explicit pending exception.
The full user-intent field split remains a separate schema direction decision.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The secrets boundary defines whether persisted material exists; catalog availability then owns the separate enablement gate before any model reader can use it.
